react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by tryptophan pathway disruption. Across three orthogonal enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 1.5×10⁻¹⁴), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p=1.0×10⁻⁶), and mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p=0.0019) — KEGG:hsa00380 / KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism emerges as the consensus winner at rank 0 in every method. Six of the nine input metabolites map to this pathway via direct compound overlap: L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), tryptamine (C00398), quinolinic acid (C03722), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632). The IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414) represents the kynurenine branch of this same system (FDR 1.4×10⁻⁸). Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) confirms the neurotransmitter arm. L-Leucine (C00123) maps independently to valine/leucine/isoleucine degradation (MetaboAnalystR) and 3-sulfinoalanine (C00606) to cysteine/methionine metabolism — these are secondary, single-tool signals. Putrescine (C00134) is a weak hit for the urea cycle/arginine-proline periphery. The data are consistent with treatment-induced skewing of tryptophan catabolism, with simultaneous dysregulation of the serotonergic branch (tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin) and the kynurenine-NAD⁺ branch (quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid).

The WikiPathways branch Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210) is independently identified by RaMP (FDR 1.1×10⁻¹⁰) and captures the kynurenine-NAD⁺ arm of tryptophan catabolism. The serotonergic arm is represented by L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin and tryptamine, while the kynurenine arm is represented by quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. L-Leucine independently hits KEGG:hsa00290 (Valine, leucine and isoleucine biosynthesis) in MetaboAnalystR.

_pathway_peek.pathway_name: Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis tools converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as its top hit with an FDR of 1.5×10⁻¹⁴, mapping 6 input metabolites including L-tryptophan (the pathway entry substrate), serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, quinolinic acid, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. Mummichog independently confirms this finding, returning MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as its top pathway (p=0.00151) with 7 input metabolites covering both the serotonergic and kynurenine branches. WikiPathways WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production) appears at rank 5 in RaMP (FDR=1.1×10⁻¹⁰), capturing the kynurenine arm via serotonin, L-tryptophan, quinolinic acid, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. Serotonin and melatonin also map to the Reactome pathway REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis, FDR=3.5×10⁻⁸). The signal is driven primarily by L-tryptophan as the metabolic entry point, with downstream products serotonin, melatonin, and the neurotoxin quinolinic acid all showing coordinated differential abundance. Cross-paradigm consensus on tryptophan pathway perturbation is strong across ORA (RaMP) and network activity (mummichog) methods.

Six of the nine input metabolites map to this pathway via direct compound overlap: L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), tryptamine (C00398), quinolinic acid (C03722), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632). The IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414) represents the kynurenine branch of this same system (FDR 1.4×10⁻⁸). Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) confirms the neurotransmitter arm. L-Leucine (C00123) maps independently to valine/leucine/isoleucine degradation (MetaboAnalystR) and 3-sulfinoalanine (C00606) to cysteine/methionine metabolism — these are secondary, single-tool signals. Putrescine (C00134) is a weak hit for the urea cycle/arginine-proline periphery.
